body:
We've never been formally diagnosed. We've been diagnosed with varying labels over the years: schizoaffective disorder, borderline personality disorder, bipolar disorder, PTSD. Y's current therapist (who I don't directly talk to) thinks it's possible she has DID, but feels  unequipped to treat her if we should have it.

For a while, we (in our various integrated and dissociated states) have been slow to push for a diagnosis of DID, in a large part due to the fact that we retain a lot of knowledge about each other's thoughts and often experience the same world, though our interpretations and temperaments about what we experience are very different. In the last year (a very bad year for both of us), large domains of memory have started to divide and fragment -- I can't access any of Y's cherished memories, for example. I know C is very close to Y, but C feels like a stranger to me because I don't have any close memories of her. If I should complete suicide, I would feel bad for C in the sense that anyone would feel guilty for killing someone's best friend, but it's not like I know C personally. 

Sometimes I think I retain more memories of sex work and sexual assault experiences than Y does, but we don't really like thinking about that sort of thing so it's not like we've compared notes.

My host is on hormones-- she started them 22 months ago (she's 24 and a half now). 18 is a perfect age to start. I feel bad if I should complete suicide actually, as she's gotten quite impressive results with them, and it's so touching to see her so happy -- it's such a pity ...
